steps: Balance equations by changing coefficients only — never change formulae
Read off the mole ratio from the balanced equation coefficients
Convert given mass to moles: moles = mass ÷ Mr
Scale moles using the ratio, then convert back: mass = moles × Mr
method_card.title: Balancing Equations and Reacting Masses
method_card.content:
Reacting mass calculations always follow the same five steps.

Step 1: Write and balance the equation.

Step 2: Identify the mole ratio of the two substances you need.

Step 3: Convert the known mass to moles: moles = mass ÷ Mr.

Step 4: Use the ratio to find moles of the unknown.

Step 5: Convert back to mass: mass = moles × Mr.

Show all five steps clearly — method marks are available even if the final arithmetic is wrong.

Common pitfalls:

  • Changing a subscript instead of a coefficient when balancing
  • Skipping the mole ratio step
  • Basing calculations on the wrong reactant when a limiting reactant is specified

exam_context.frequency: High — reacting mass questions appear in most chemistry papers

gold.display: In 2Al + 3Cl2 → 2AlCl3, calculate the mass of AlCl3 produced from 27 g of Al. (Mr: Al = 27, AlCl3 = 133.5)

misconceptions.message: Moles Al = 27/27 = 1 mol. Ratio 2:2 = 1:1. Mass AlCl3 = 1 × 133.5 = 133.5 g.

gold.display: In 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O, calculate the mass of water produced from 4 g of H2. (Mr: H2 = 2, H2O = 18)

misconceptions.message: Moles H2 = 4/2 = 2 mol. Ratio 2:2 = 1:1. Mass H2O = 2 × 18 = 36 g.

gold.display: Methane combustion: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O. Calculate the mass of CO2 produced from 32 g of CH4. (Mr: CH4 = 16, CO2 = 44)

misconceptions.message: Moles CH4 = 32/16 = 2 mol. Ratio 1:1 so 2 mol CO2. Mass = 2 × 44 = 88 g.

bronze.display: In CuCO3 → CuO + CO2, what mass of CuO is produced from 62 g of CuCO3? (Mr: CuCO3 = 124, CuO = 80)
bronze.equation_hint: Moles = mass ÷ Mr, then use 1:1 ratio, then mass = moles × Mr

misconceptions.message: Moles CuCO3 = 62/124 = 0.5. Ratio 1:1 so 0.5 mol CuO. Mass = 0.5 × 80 = 40 g.

bronze.display: In 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO, what mass of MgO is produced from 24 g of Mg? (Mr: Mg = 24, MgO = 40)

misconceptions.message: Moles Mg = 24/24 = 1 mol. Ratio 1:1 so 1 mol MgO. Mass = 1 × 40 = 40 g.

bronze.display: In CaCO3 → CaO + CO2, what mass of CO2 is produced from 100 g of CaCO3? (Mr: CaCO3 = 100, CO2 = 44)

misconceptions.message: Moles CaCO3 = 100/100 = 1 mol. Ratio 1:1. Mass CO2 = 1 × 44 = 44 g.

bronze.display: How many moles are in 56 g of iron? (Ar of Fe = 56)
In 2Na + 2H2O → 2NaOH + H2, how many moles of H2 are produced from 2 mol of Na?

misconceptions.message: Ratio 2:1 — 2 mol Na gives 1 mol H2.

silver.display: In 4Fe + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3, calculate the mass of Fe2O3 produced from 56 g of iron. (Mr: Fe = 56, Fe2O3 = 160)

misconceptions.message: Moles Fe = 1 mol. Ratio 4:2 = 2:1, so 0.5 mol Fe2O3. Mass = 0.5 × 160 = 80 g.

silver.display: In N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3, calculate the mass of ammonia produced from 28 g of N2. (Mr: N2 = 28, NH3 = 17)

misconceptions.message: Moles N2 = 1 mol. Ratio 1:2, so 2 mol NH3. Mass = 2 × 17 = 34 g.

silver.display: In N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3, calculate the mass of ammonia produced from 6 g of H2. (Mr: H2 = 2, NH3 = 17)

misconceptions.message: Moles H2 = 6/2 = 3 mol. Ratio 3:2 so 2 mol NH3. Mass = 2 × 17 = 34 g.

silver.display: Zinc reacts with oxygen: 2Zn + O2 → 2ZnO. Calculate the mass of ZnO produced from 13 g of Zn. (Mr: Zn = 65, ZnO = 81)

misconceptions.message: Moles Zn = 13/65 = 0.2 mol. Ratio 1:1. Mass ZnO = 0.2 × 81 = 16.2 g.
